newsitem.title: UK: W&P plan 150 more Alldays stores in 1997.
newsitem.headline: W&P plan 150 more Alldays stores in 1997.

text.p: British food retailer Watson & Philip said it plans to open over 150 Alldays stores in 1997 after the 526-strong chain reported like-for-like sales up 2.2 percent in the year to October 27, 1996.

The convenience food store chain also boasted an operating margin of 5.4 percent in the year up from 4.9 percent. Chief executive Colin Glass, pledged to increase the Alldays' network of stores to 1,000 by the millenium.
The company's shares soared 42-1/2p in early trade to 383p.

In the first few weeks of this financial year, like-for-like sales in Alldays are "running slightly ahead of a very buoyant period last year," said chairman James Watson in a statement attached to the company's full year results.

The planned opening of 150 stores will include the recently announced franchise agreement with Total Oil Ltd which will lead to some 50 Total owned petrol forecourts being converted to incorporate an Alldays store at Total's cost.
"Today's convenience shoppper expects, and is getting from Alldays, higher quality combined with an appropriate range of products and this provides higher margin opportunity," said Watson.

Alldays improved operating profit 25 percent to 15.1 million in the year. The company's food service business increased trading profit by 19 percent to 4.0 million on turnover which leapt 40 percent to 166 million.
W&P's foodservice division reported a like-for-like sales increase of 20 percent.

"The food service market place continues to expand in line with expectations and is already the UK's fourth largest consumer market and within it, certain sectors, including themed restaurants and leisure are growing at a very significant rate," said Watson.
The group reported an 11 percent increase in pretax, pre-exceptional profit to 20.1 million in the year. An exceptional charge of 1.3 million related mainly to losses on the sale of properties.
